The bus
doesn't
lie.

CANarchy is an open, stream-first runtime for analyzing and manipulating CAN and J1939 buses. Every command emits a canonical JSONL event. Every event is replayable. Nothing is hidden behind a GUI, a license key, or a dongle.

WHAT THIS IS
A toolkit for security researchers, red teams,
fleet auditors, OSS tinkerers, and the
occasional agent operating without supervision.

WHAT IT IS NOT
A replacement for can-utils, python-can,
SavvyCAN, or common sense.

SIX
MOVES.

CORE SUBCOMMANDS
all composable · all emit events
NO.01● STABLE

STREAM

JSONL events. Stable schema. Pipe to grep, jq, duckdb, or your agent. The CLI *is* the API.

NO.02● STABLE

J1939

Heavy vehicles are not an afterthought. PGNs, TP reassembly, address claim — first-class.

NO.03● STABLE

UDS

Discover services. Trace transactions. Every active command is gated behind --ack-active, --dry-run, and a typed YES.

NO.04● STABLE

DBC

Provider-backed discovery. Local cache. Reverse-engineering matchers when you only have frames.

NO.05● STABLE

GATEWAY

Bridge buses. Rewrite frames in flight. Replay captures with real timing or compressed.

NO.06● STABLE

AGENT

Deterministic subcommands. MCP server. Build loops with Claude, Cursor, or anything that can shell out.

◉ LIVE TAPE · can0 @ 250K
// EXHIBIT A — ONE PIPELINE, ONE TRUTH

CAPTURE. DECODE.
COMPARE. REPLAY.

# STEP 1 — CAPTURE + DECODE
$ canarchy capture can0 --jsonl \
    | canarchy j1939 decode --stdin --jsonl

{"ts":"17:42:19.20","pgn":61444,
 "name":"EEC1","engine_rpm":1842.25}
{"ts":"17:42:19.22","pgn":61444,
 "name":"EEC1","engine_rpm":1847.00}
{"ts":"17:42:19.24","pgn":65262,
 "name":"ET1", "coolant_c":88}
# STEP 2 — COMPARE AGAINST BASELINE
$ canarchy j1939 compare \
    baseline.candump run.candump \
    --text

unique_pgns:
- run.candump: 65262[ET1]
dm1_differences:
- sa=0x00 [Engine #1]
  run.candump: present=True faults=spn=110/fmi=3
  baseline.candump: present=False faults=none

AGENT TRANSCRIPT · LIVEclaude ↔ canarchy
USER Audit the truck on can0 for 10s and flag anything that looks like an unsolicited diagnostic session.
↳ agent decides to capture, then filter for UDS traffic before deciding whether an active probe is warranted
→ call capture
{ "interface": "can0", "duration": 10, "decode": "j1939" }
← {"command":"capture","ok":true,"data":{...}} … 428 events
→ call filter
{ "expression": "name~=UDS.*", "file": "$last" }
← 3 matching events — all sa=0x27
AGENT Flagged 3 uds.session.request from sa=0x27. No active probe attempted over MCP — that requires `canarchy uds scan can0`, gated behind --ack-active and a typed YES.
DETERMINISTIC
Same inputs in, same JSONL out. Agents can loop without drift.
STREAMING
Tools return event streams. No 10k-token blobs, no truncation.
DRY-RUN BY DEFAULT
Active commands require explicit --ack-active plus a typed YES. Guard framework (speed / ignition / session, marked PLANNED in the MCP catalog above) is on the roadmap.

▣ INSTALL / RUN

THREE
COMMANDS.
ZERO FLUFF.

Plug in a USB CAN interface, point it at a log file, or spin up a virtual bus. You’ll have your first JSONL event before your coffee is cold.

$ ZSH · canarchy v0.7.0
# 1. install
➜ pip install canarchy

# 2. check your environment
➜ canarchy doctor --text

# 3. stream + decode J1939 events as JSONL
➜ canarchy capture can0 --jsonl | canarchy j1939 decode --stdin --jsonl

# 4. (optional) let an agent drive it
➜ canarchy mcp serve
